body.statement: For every \(N\), \(\inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}P_X^N\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N\}\ge1-\alpha\). On the simultaneous covariance event, \(\operatorname{ex}(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))\le4L_\beta\Delta_N\). This is a finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber guarantee unavailable from Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 of Wang--Kolar--Drton: those results start from an asymptotically valid confidence set for a true ordering and asymptotically valid conditional adjustment-set intervals to cover one total effect, whereas \(C_N\) contains every element of the partially identified fiber on one event. The underlying regimes are nonnested: \(\mathcal M\setminus\mathcal W_{\mathrm{WKD}}\ne\varnothing\) because generic common non-Gaussian source loadings on multiple coordinates yield latent dependence that violates their mutually independent additive-error representation and its residual--regressor order certificate, while \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{WKD}}\setminus\mathcal M\ne\varnothing\) because identifiable additive-error laws may have characteristic-function zeros on a named ray or no positive Gaussian divisor and hence violate the maintained Fourier lower envelope or \(\Gamma\succeq\lambda I\).
body.justification: The theorem supplies finite-sample simultaneous coverage of the complete mixed-noise effect fiber, rather than asymptotic coverage of one effect after order-confidence and adjustment-set steps.
body.gap: Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 work in a causally sufficient recursive additive-error model with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and order identifiability from nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors; their effect interval is asymptotically valid for one total effect conditional on order-set and adjustment-interval validity. The present nonnested model permits latent common sources, identifies a greatest Gaussian divisor by Fourier tails, and gives finite-sample simultaneous inclusion of every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect.
body.consumer: The \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) workflow can report a confidence-enlarged set of all compatible effects rather than a selected list.
